paragraphs: Friend, here's the biggest thing in this passage. Joseph looks at the brothers who sold him and says, "it was to save lives that God sent me before you" (Genesis 45:5). He doesn't pretend it didn't happen, because he says it plainly: "the one you sold into Egypt!" (Genesis 45:4). But he sees something bigger than their sin, which is that God was working the whole time.

Now watch what that does. Joseph tells them, "do not be distressed or angry with yourselves" (Genesis 45:5), and then he feeds them, loads them with wagons and sends them home with the best of Egypt (Genesis 45:18-21). That's what forgiveness looks like when it's real. It doesn't hold the grudge, and it doesn't make people crawl. I have been stuffed in a drawer and forgotten, so trust me, I know what it's worth when somebody opens the door and welcomes you in instead of keeping score.

So here's what I want you to take to the oven today, baker. When someone has hurt you, or when you've hurt somebody and it's eating you up, remember that God can work in the middle of it and He is not finished. Joseph could forgive because he saw God's hand in it, and you can start there too. And this family's story still has a whole lot more in the oven, so stay close.
